detail.quote: Then $Y = \bar{X}_n$. Then $Y \sim \text{Normal}(\mu, \sigma^2)$, where $\mu = np$ and $\sigma^2 = np(1-p)$.
detail.explanation: Those are the mean and variance of the head count $X$, not the observed proportion $\bar X_n=X/n$. The proportion has mean $p$ and variance $p(1-p)/n$. The subsequent standardization therefore uses the wrong distribution, so the boxed answer is not supported. The candidate also assumes $p=0.5$ without justification, though the distributional error occurs first.
